dedupe_keys.name: capri common agricultural policy regionalised impact modelling system

description: CAPRI is an agricultural sector model covering the whole EU27, Norway and the Western Balkans at regional level (250 regions), and global agricultural markets at country or country-block level. It is used to simulate and compare, ex ante over about 8 to 15 years, the effects of agricultural policies, and for longer climate change projections. It is comparative-static, with regional supply models that maximise profit and a global market model of about 40,000 simultaneous equations with bilateral trade flows, transport costs and tariffs. Results cover crop areas and herd sizes, input and output coefficients and incomes by activity and region, prices, supply, demand and trade, nitrogen, phosphorus and potassium balances, ammonia, methane and nitrous oxide emissions, policy costs and welfare. Coverage: EU regional, global markets. Access: CAPRI is handled as open source and is written in GAMS, so changing it needs a GAMS licence; access rights are set on the versioning server, and some project results stay client-only for a time. It is maintained by a network of users and developers, with a coordinating team in Bonn, a wiki, stable releases, and training through Humboldt University and the Thünen Institute. Caveats: no named licence was found on the pages read, and the model runs no yearly dynamics. For simulation it projects how climate, trade or policy shocks change EU agricultural production, prices and emissions. Related catalogue records include MAgPIE, GLOBIOM, IFPRI IMPACT and GTAP.
